card.name: The word risk in warning statements
card.fires_on: The word "risk" or "risks" (or "at" just before "increased risk") in drug warnings that tell readers to consider, be aware of, or inform patients about a risk. It comes right before "of", "for" or "when" and the named harm.

modes.label: The prompt to consider these risks
modes.description: "Risks" in the spinal hematoma warning, just before "when scheduling patients".
modes.example: Consider these<< risks>> when scheduling patients for spinal procedures.

modes.label: Risk of a named harm
modes.description: "Risk" after "the" or "increased" in advice to inform or monitor patients, followed by a named adverse effect.
modes.example: inform patients of the increased<< risk>> for serotonin syndrome and monitor for symptoms.

card.plain: It responds to the word "risk" in warnings that point to a harm which is about to be named.
